notes.title: Ask your library and Apple Watch capture
items: Mac and iPhone: ask your library a question in plain words, such as “What did Alex want changed on the homepage?” Verbose finds the passages that match on your device, then Apple Intelligence answers from those passages only. Each sentence cites the recording and the time it came from.

Mac: press ⌘K anywhere in Verbose, or click Search or ask at the top of the sidebar, to open one field for both. Switch to Search to filter the Library as before, or to Ask for an answer. In the Native look, the toolbar's search field asks when you press Return.

Mac: click a citation to play the recording from that time without leaving the answer. Right-click it to open the transcript at that line. On iPhone, tap a citation to open the transcript at that line and play it.

Mac and iPhone: choose where Ask looks: All, This week (the last seven days), Thoughts, Meetings, or a project. If nothing there matches, Verbose says so instead of guessing. Without Apple Intelligence, you get the matching passages and the reason.

Mac and iPhone: Copy puts the answer and its sources on the clipboard, and Save as recipe keeps the question and where it looks. Ask is under Make in the Mac's sidebar, and in Library › Ask on iPhone. On iPhone, the Library's search field offers Ask about what you typed.

Mac and iPhone: recipes are questions you ask again. Run one now, or schedule it weekly on that device; its answers stay in Ask › Recipes with their citations. Recipes sync between your Mac and iPhone, and schedules stay on each device. Start from three suggestions, such as Weekly digest of my thoughts.

Mac and iPhone: a scheduled recipe runs while Verbose is open, or the next time it opens after its time, once even if you missed several weeks. On iPhone, it can also run when iOS gives Verbose background time. You get a notification with the first line of the answer.
Mac and iPhone: Ask's index stays on your device and updates in the background as your transcripts change, never while you record or transcribe. Nothing from your transcripts leaves your device.

Mac and iPhone: when you delete a recording or move it to Recently Deleted, Ask forgets its passages at once, and saved answers drop its citations. Delete all data also removes Ask's index, your recent questions, recipes, and their answers.

Apple Watch: record a voice note or a thought from your wrist. Tap Record or New thought, mark moments while you record, then tap Stop. Your iPhone transcribes it and adds it to the Library, or to today's Thoughts with Apple Watch as where it came from. The Apple Watch app needs watchOS 11.

Apple Watch: tap Mark, or double-tap your fingers on a watch that supports it, to mark a moment. Your wrist gets a tap and the watch says “Marked 4:12”. In the transcript, the moment says “from the Apple Watch”.

Apple Watch: recording keeps going when you lower your wrist. When your iPhone is out of reach, the watch keeps the recording and sends it once your iPhone is back, and shows how many recordings are waiting.
Apple Watch: add Record and Today's thoughts to your watch face, and find your last recording in the Smart Stack. Each one opens Verbose ready to record.

iPhone: touch and hold Record to open Record as, a tray with six ways to record: Voice note, Meeting, Interview, Journal entry, Talk, and Thought. Slide your finger to one and lift to start it, or lift in place and tap one. It opens from Home's Record card in both looks and from the floating record button in the Native look.

iPhone: each row in Record as says what happens when the recording finishes, such as “Runs Meeting notes when it finishes” when Run automatically has a template for that kind. Voice note leaves the kind to Verbose, and Thought adds to today's page, as New thought does. Record a note is gone from the list.

iPhone: the recorder shows the kind you picked in a chip, and the line under the timer names the template that runs when you stop. In the Native look, the floating record button's Dictate, Live captions, and Import sit in a row under the kinds.

iPhone: with VoiceOver, Record has an action for each way to record, each row in the tray is a button, and the escape gesture closes the tray. With larger text, the rows grow and scroll when the tray gets tall.

Mac: right-click Record, or choose File › Record As, for the same six choices, each with its Verbose icon: Record, Record a meeting, Record an interview, Record a journal entry, Record a talk, and New thought. File › Record As › Meeting… starts a meeting recording, in place of the separate Record Meeting… item.

iPhone: the Library opens with one row of tiles for Dictations, By day, Templates, and Ask, so your recordings start higher up. The type chips stay in place when you pick a kind, and kinds, Pinned, In progress, and projects have a row of their own.

iPhone: a thought that's still transcribing shows Thought and its time instead of a blank title, and thought times in Verbose style show morning or afternoon, such as 10:00a and 3:00p. The Journal tab no longer switches itself to Thoughts.

iPhone: a transcript hides the tab bar while you read, and the player's play button and progress are sage. The header has one meta line; tap the data path chip for the source, engine, and time. The Cleaned tab's Clean up chip stays on one line.

iPhone: Dictations, Add from Library, Moments, You, Settings › Keyboard, About me, Your voice, and the Action button page use the same chips, rows, titles, and colors as the rest of the app. The keyboard session screens make going back to your app the main step.
Mac and iPhone: a transcript without a kind shows a Kind menu, and Add a tag says Tag until you add one. While a link downloads, its card offers Cancel download and Keep downloading.

Mac and iPhone: the 1:1 template has its own icon, and the Dictionary tile in the Native look no longer shares Journal's symbol. On iPhone, What's new lists what you can use on this iPhone first and folds Mac-only items under On your Mac.
iPhone: screens, tabs, and rows appear at once, without rising or sliding in.

iPhone: a Haptics switch in Settings › Personalization and preferences turns off every tap Verbose plays, in the app, in the Verbose keyboard, and on your Apple Watch. Delete all data no longer buzzes.

iPhone: Record gives a gentle tap just before the microphone turns on, and Stop or Discard gives a softer tap the moment you tap it, instead of a buzz after saving. This works for voice notes, thoughts, Live captions, and keyboard sessions.
iPhone: Pause, Resume, and Mark tap while you record. Before, iOS silenced every tap while the microphone was on, so most recording taps never played.

iPhone: when a transcript is ready with Verbose open, you feel one success tap per recording, even when a template runs after it. When something goes wrong, such as the microphone not being allowed or a recording that can't be saved, you feel an error tap; an automatic pause or low storage gives a warning tap.
iPhone: every Copy, including transcripts, Ask, Actions, Export, Copy for AI, and Thoughts, gives the same light tick, as does a ribbon take that's copied or inserted.

iPhone: in the Verbose keyboard, starting a dictation and tapping Done give the same taps as Record and Stop in the app, and follow Verbose's Haptics switch. Typing keys tap only when you turn on Settings › Keyboard › Typing haptics. Keyboard taps need Allow Full Access.

Apple Watch: the taps for start, Mark, Stop, and a recording that can't start follow the Haptics switch on your iPhone. The start tap plays before the microphone turns on, so it isn't in the recording.

iPhone: in Verbose style, Settings icons are neutral, Home's tiles take their color from what they do (Dictate butter, Import sage, What's playing petal) wherever you put them, and every button is a pill.
iPhone: Recent recordings on Home lists your newest recordings first, by when you made them, as the Library does.

iPhone: the Verbose style recorder puts Mark moment, Stop & transcribe, and Pause in the thumb row, as Premium Native does, shows your last two moments under the meter, and moves Discard under the row. Live words while you record start on a whole word.

iPhone: smaller fixes. Voice notes have one name everywhere, Native uses sentence case and large titles on Settings pages, the Library's count is the system's tab badge, the Saved sheet keeps Open transcript as its one filled button, Home shows a person icon until you add your name, and Edit Home, the tab bar picker, and Today's thoughts no longer cut off their labels.

Mac Home: the Dictate tile's Accessibility note wraps and ends with Open Accessibility settings. Edit Home shows each section's full name, with Choose tiles as a pill and one Done. Last dictation shows up to three lines, even after a greeting's blank line. In the Native look, the tiles go two by two in a narrower window so names and statuses aren't cut off, the greeting fades under the toolbar, and the toolbar keeps Back, Forward, and Import in the same place on every screen.

Mac Library: Thoughts get a neutral dot, since persimmon means recording. Text-only thoughts say Text instead of a zero length. Voice notes have one name everywhere. Recently deleted, the link card, and Add from Library use the same pills and chips as the rest of the app, and Add from Library has the Library's kind chips. Thoughts in the Library link to Read by day. Dictations say Cleaned once, and an app whose icon can't load shows a neutral glyph. Link dates leave out this year.
Mac: the app audio picker explains what permission Verbose needs and opens System Settings for you, then fills in the list when you come back.

Mac transcripts: the play button and the played part of the waveform are sage, the playback color. Run a template sits in the tool row, every tool has a name for VoiceOver, and a short title fits on one line. Speaker colors follow who talks first, matching the multi-track sheet. Lines fade under the player. The Export sheet fits the window, with pill buttons and the file's name as it's saved. In the Native look, a row says when a template result is ready in the closed inspector.

Mac Templates: a row's name gets the whole line, with Runs for in the line below. The editor puts Cancel and Save at the right, scrolls when it's tall, and wraps its kind chips. Templates and Actions point to each other. In the Native look, only New Template uses the accent.

Mac Moments: every filter shows its count, a new Marked filter shows moments you marked while recording, and the intro mentions marking while you record. Where a mark came from reads the same on the transcript and in Moments, such as Mac · ⌃⌥B.

Mac: Thoughts' By day keeps Open as pad on one line and the Native sidebar in place, folds thoughts where nothing was heard into one row you can delete, and moves a stray press under 1.4 seconds with nothing heard to Recently Deleted. The sidebar counts today's thoughts and this week's journal entries, New thought is an outlined pill with its shortcut, and the floating page outlines only the newest thought.

Mac: in Settings, Watched folders no longer runs off the window with a long Save to path, the first pane is Personalization in the sidebar, the Fn key's setup step reads as a step until you choose Fn, Actions show Verbose's own icons, and Support's buttons use sentence case. You stacks its first row in a narrow window, and the welcome tour's last step asks about languages, then speed or accuracy.

Mac: the floating button's Stop no longer cuts off, the notch's Remember is paper on black with your project named in the message, Return in Recent dictations pastes as its Paste button says, and Live captions says what it's listening to until the first words arrive.

Mac: buttons, switches, links, and selections look the same across Verbose style: pills in sheets, toasts, onboarding, and Recently Deleted; one view switch for Templates, By day, Export, and You; ink text links; a leading plus on create buttons; and the outlined card for a selected row. Premium Native's warm glow fades out without a hard edge, and the on-device note reads the same in Templates, Ask, and You.

Mac: the Native look follows macOS 27, where Apple took brand color out of its own apps. Everything you click takes your Mac's accent color from System Settings › Appearance, blue by default, and red marks only recording. The warm background, glow, gradient cards, and shadows are gone.

Mac: in the Native look, Record is a toolbar button. Click it to record a voice note, or click its arrow for Dictate, Live captions, Import, and the six ways to record. The floating record button is gone, so it never covers a row.

Mac: in the Native look, the Library opens as a table with Name, Kind, People or source, Date, and Length. Click a column's heading to sort by it. Switch to List in the toolbar to see what was said in each recording.

Mac: in the Native look, a transcript reads in a centered column with Original and Cleaned in the toolbar, and the player is a glass bar with the waveform as its scrubber. Review Changes, Mark This Moment, and Text Size are in the toolbar's More menu.
Mac: in the Native look, Home shows your quick actions, This week, and your recent recordings as grouped sections, and the Settings window shows each pane with a colored icon, like System Settings.
iPhone: a quick tap on Record starts a voice note again. Touch and hold still opens Record as.

iPhone: the Native look follows Apple's own apps more closely. Buttons, links, tabs, switches you turn on, and selection use the system accent (blue), red appears only for recording, and screens use the system's backgrounds, with no gradient cards, glows, or custom shadows.

iPhone: in the Native look, Record sits in the tab bar's bottom accessory on every tab. Tap it to record a voice note, or touch and hold it to record a meeting, an interview, a journal entry, a talk, or a thought, or to dictate, open Live captions, or import. While you record, it shows the time with Pause and Stop, and a tap brings the recorder back.

iPhone: in the Native look, the recorder is a sheet like Voice Memos', with a large clock, a waveform under a red playhead, your words as they're heard, and Mark moment, Stop, and Pause. Swipe it down and the recording keeps going in the tab bar.

iPhone: in the Native look, Home is a list like Apple's own apps, with the date under the large title. Quick actions are rows with blue symbols, This week is one cell with the words, recordings, time saved, and the seven days, and recent recordings show what was said. The Record card setting is gone, because Record is always in the tab bar.

iPhone: in the Native look, the Library is a plain list like Mail's inbox. Dictations, Projects, By day, Templates, and Ask are rows at the top, and each recording shows its title and time, its kind, length, and names, and two lines of what was said. The filter button opens a menu with what to show, Sort by, and Select recordings, and fills while a filter is on. Recently Deleted is in the More menu.

iPhone: in the Native look, a transcript keeps two controls beside Back: Share, and More, a menu built like Apple Books' with Copy, Find, and Mark on top, then Summary, Moments, Speakers, Run a template, Actions, Export, Add to project, Text and display, Details, Rename, and Delete. Find lists the lines that match and plays from the one you tap.
iPhone: in the Native look, a transcript's player is a glass bar at the bottom with the waveform as its scrubber, the time left, the speed, and Follow.
iPhone: in the Native look, Settings shows each row's symbol in white on a colored square, like Apple's Settings app, and switches are green.
iPhone: in the Native look, the keyboard session's screens, search highlights, and the playing line use system colors instead of persimmon.

iPhone: in the Native look, Moments has a large title with the count under it and a segmented control for what to show, You shows your week, year, and stats as plain list sections, Today's page puts New thought in the toolbar, and the Tab bar preview shows Record above the tabs.
iPhone and Mac: in the Native look, widgets are black, like Apple Music's, with white text and the red record disc as the only color, in light and dark mode.
iPhone: with the Native look, the Verbose keyboard uses the system's blue for Tap to talk, the voice bars, and Done, with white text, like the system keyboard.

Mac and iPhone: Record as has two new ways to record, after Thought. Audio only keeps the sound and makes no transcript, for a melody you hum, a guitar part, or a room you want to remember. Brain dump records you talking through your day, and Plan my day sorts it into a plan when it finishes.

Mac and iPhone: Audio only records with the system's voice processing off, so music keeps its dynamics. It has its own screen with a player, a title you type, the moments you marked, and notes. In the Library, its row shows the waveform with a play button, so you can listen without opening it.

Mac and iPhone: to get words from an Audio only recording later, choose Transcribe on its screen or in its Library menu. It becomes a voice note, and its title, notes, moments, and audio stay. Touch and hold Transcribe on iPhone, or open its menu on the Mac, to transcribe it as a meeting, a brain dump, or another kind.

Mac and iPhone: Plan my day is a new template with Top three, Today, Tomorrow, This week, Someday, and Ideas. It uses only the days you said, counted from when you recorded, and each task links to the moment you said it. Brain dump runs it automatically from the start; you can turn that off in Run automatically.

Mac and iPhone: Send to Reminders adds a plan's tasks to the Reminders list you pick. A task gets a due date only when you said a day, and ideas go in only if you check them. Tasks you've sent are marked, so sending again adds only what's new.
Mac and iPhone: Organize today's thoughts makes the same plan from all of a day's thoughts, and each task links back to the thought it came from. On the Mac, it's Organize on today's page.

Mac: File › New Brain Dump opens a note for today. Hold your dictation keys and talk, or type, then choose Make a plan. Dictations into the note stay in the note and aren't listed in Dictations. The menu bar's Thoughts group and an optional Home tile open it too.

Mac and iPhone: you can change any recording's kind to Brain dump or Audio only later, and back. Changing a kind never deletes the transcript, notes, or results. Changing one to Brain dump offers to run Plan my day.

Mac and iPhone: Audio only records at your microphone's own rate, 48 or 44.1 kHz, in 24-bit, so a guitar or a voice keeps its high end. Voice notes and other kinds still record at 16 kHz. Transcribe later and sharing work with the new files.

iPhone: in dark mode, the Lock Screen's recording and dictation session sit on Verbose's dark green instead of bright paper. When a call pauses a thought, the Lock Screen and the Dynamic Island offer Resume beside Stop.

iPhone: a recording longer than an hour shows its full time in the Dynamic Island and on the Lock Screen, and every Live Activity button is a pill. VoiceOver and Voice Control use the words the buttons show, such as Done and Dictate.
iPhone: Verbose's Control Center controls use Verbose's own icons, and the Action button's control is named for what you chose in Settings › Action button, such as Record or mark.

iPhone: widget names are clearer (Record and dictate, Today's thoughts, and Thoughts for the Lock Screen), and small labels on widgets and in the keyboard are larger and in full ink. The small Record widget says Voice note, which is what it records.
iPhone: in the Native look in dark mode, the keyboard's Start, Tap to talk, and Done are black on the persimmon so they're readable, and VoiceOver reads the keyboard's checkmark as Done.

notes.title: Templates, Mark a moment, and the Mac catches up: Back, clearer noisy transcripts, and Thoughts and Journal on Home
items: Mac: a Back button on every transcript returns you to the Library right where you were, with the same row, search, and filters. ⌘[ works too.
Mac: the Library no longer jumps back to the top a moment after Back returns you to it.

Mac: Actions › Transcribe again with Whisper Turbo listens to the recording again with a bigger model. It's slower, and it hears names and noisy stretches better. The first time, it downloads the model (1.6 GB).
Mac and iPhone: after Transcribe again with Whisper Turbo, your speaker names, notes, and moments stay, and Actions › Switch to puts the earlier words back.
Mac and iPhone: where speech was too hard to hear, the transcript shows a quiet “unclear 2:10” chip. Click or tap it to play that spot. Words the engine wasn't sure of have a dotted underline.
Mac and iPhone: Export can add “[unclear 2:10]” markers. They're off unless you turn on Unclear markers.
Mac and iPhone: Reduce background noise in the player's speed menu turns down wind or a mower while you listen. It doesn't change the transcript or the recording.
Mac and iPhone: Edit Home adds Today's thoughts (your latest thoughts with their times, and New thought) and Journal (your newest entry with a play button, and this week's days). Both start hidden.
Mac and iPhone: two new Home tiles. New thought records a thought without leaving Home, and Journal opens Journal by day. On the Mac, the floating Thoughts tile is now called Today's page.

Mac and iPhone: templates turn a transcript into notes, a plan, or a draft. Pick one of the five built-in actions, one of eight scenarios such as Meeting notes, 1:1, Interview, and Daily reflection, or your own. On the Mac, open Templates under Make in the sidebar. On iPhone, open Library › Templates.

Mac and iPhone: make your own template from a name, plain instructions, and the sections you want back, each a paragraph, bullets, a checklist, or quotes with times. Try it on a recording before you save it. Your templates sync between your Mac and iPhone.

Mac and iPhone: Run automatically gives each kind of recording one template, so every Meeting can get Meeting notes when it finishes. It runs after the transcript and summary, once per recording, and skips recordings under 2 minutes unless you turn that off. Each device keeps its own choices, and every kind starts Off.

Mac and iPhone: a template's result stays in the transcript with why it ran, Run again, and Edit. On iPhone, it's a tab beside Original and Cleaned. Templates use only what the transcript says and run on your device with Apple Intelligence.

Mac and iPhone: start a recording as a kind. Touch and hold Record on iPhone and choose Record a meeting, an interview, a journal entry, a talk, or a note; on the Mac, right-click Record. Verbose keeps the kind you pick, and Run automatically uses it. On the Mac, Shortcuts' Start recording takes a kind too.

Mac and iPhone: when you change a recording's kind after its template ran, the result asks, for example, “Now a Journal. Run Daily reflection?” Nothing runs until you choose Run, and the old result stays until then.

iPhone: mark a moment while you record, without opening Verbose. Tap Mark in the expanded Dynamic Island or in the Lock Screen's recording, or on the recorder. The Island says “Marked 4:12” with how many moments you've marked, and the Lock Screen shows your last mark.
iPhone: the Lock Screen's recording sits on paper with your voice, Mark, Pause, and Stop.

iPhone: Settings › Action button has a new choice, Record or mark. Press once to start a voice note; while it records, each press marks a moment. Set up the Action button shows the three steps in the Settings app.

Mac: mark a moment while you record. Click Mark on Home's record panel or on the bubble's card, or press ⌃⌥B in any app. With nothing recording, ⌃⌥B does nothing. Change it in Settings › Dictation and keyboard › Mark a moment.
Mac: the Thoughts bubble shows a voice note while it records, with your words and Mark. Click the disc to stop it.

Mac and iPhone: each mark becomes a moment on the line you were saying, quoting its first sentence, with a chip such as “Moment 4:12 · from the Lock Screen”. Moments show where each mark came from, and marks sync with the transcript. On the Mac, right-click a moment and choose Rename to use your own words.

notes.title: iPhone only: your own tab bar and Home sections
items: iPhone: the Action button set to Dictate no longer risks closing Verbose when it starts a session. The session's Live Activity shows first, or Verbose asks before it turns on the microphone.

iPhone: choose your tabs in Settings › Personalization and preferences › Tab bar. Home stays first and Settings last; pick up to three between them from Library, Thoughts, Journal, Moments, Dictations, and Projects, and drag to reorder. Edit Home has a Tab bar link too.
iPhone: the Thoughts tab opens today's page, and the Journal tab opens Journal by day. Each tab keeps its own place. Links to a tab you removed open inside Library or Home.
Mac and iPhone: Edit Home adds Today's thoughts (your latest thoughts with their times, and New thought) and Journal (your newest entry with a play button, and this week's days). Both start hidden.
Mac and iPhone: two new Home tiles. New thought records a thought without leaving Home, and Journal opens Journal by day. On the Mac, the floating Thoughts tile is now called Today's page.

notes.title: iPhone only: clearer noisy transcripts and a widget fix
items: iPhone: Actions › Transcribe again with Whisper Turbo sends the recording to your Mac. The transcript says “Waiting for your Mac” until the new words are in.
Mac and iPhone: after Transcribe again with Whisper Turbo, your speaker names, notes, and moments stay, and Actions › Switch to puts the earlier words back.
Mac and iPhone: where speech was too hard to hear, the transcript shows a quiet “unclear 2:10” chip. Click or tap it to play that spot. Words the engine wasn't sure of have a dotted underline.
Mac and iPhone: Export can add “[unclear 2:10]” markers. They're off unless you turn on Unclear markers.
Mac and iPhone: Reduce background noise in the player's speed menu turns down wind or a mower while you listen. It doesn't change the transcript or the recording.
iPhone: AirPods record in higher quality on iOS 26, instead of over the phone-call link.
iPhone: tapping the New thought widget no longer closes Verbose. The thought records behind its Live Activity, or Verbose opens to the recorder.

notes.title: Thoughts on the iPhone
items: iPhone: Thoughts. Tap New thought on today's page and say a thought. It lands on today's page with its time, like on the Mac.

iPhone: start a thought without opening Verbose from the New thought widget, the Lock Screen, Control Center, the Action button, or Siri (“New thought in Verbose”). The Dynamic Island shows your voice, your words, and Stop.
iPhone: every thought is saved as audio before it's transcribed, so none is lost. If transcription fails, tap Transcribe again.
iPhone: Library › By day shows Thoughts and Journal one page a day, with a calendar that marks the days you recorded. Use the arrows on a page to read earlier days, and tap a thought to edit it.
iPhone: the Quick capture widget is now New thought, and the new Today's thoughts widget shows today's last two thoughts. The Lock Screen widget shows only how many, never your words.
iPhone: Settings › Features › Thoughts shows each way in and how to set up the Action button and Back Tap.
iPhone: the Action button can start a thought. Choose New thought in Settings › Action button.

notes.title: Faster By day and look switching
items: Mac: Library › By day opens faster in Native, and switching looks no longer redraws the closed Thoughts page.

notes.title: Thoughts on the Mac
items: Mac: switching between Home, Library, and You is instant, with no overlap.
Mac: Thoughts. Click the floating bubble or press ⌃⌥P in any app to say a thought, and click again to keep it. It lands on today's page with its time, and the app you're in stays in front.
Mac: every thought is saved as audio before it's transcribed, so none is lost. If transcription fails, choose Transcribe again.
Mac: the Thought pad is now today's Thoughts page. Use its arrows to read earlier days. What was on your pad moved to the days you wrote it.
Mac: Library › By day shows Thoughts and Journal one page a day, with a calendar that marks the days you recorded.
Mac: the Quick capture widget is now New thought, which starts a thought without opening Verbose, and a new Today's thoughts widget shows today's page.
Mac: a dictation that doesn't paste is kept in Dictations, and ⌃⌘V still pastes it again.
The Idea kind is now called Thoughts.
Settings shows the version as 1.0 beta with the build number, and What's new groups builds by version.

notes.title: More words spelled right
items: Verbose spells about 330 more words right without any setup: AI tools and apps, places, people, brands, film and video gear, and business terms, such as NVIDIA, Albuquerque, H.264, and EBITDA.
Dictation fixes everyday mix-ups that are always wrong, such as “could of been” and “sneak peak.” Turn them off with Built-in vocabulary in Settings.

notes.title: Snappier on the Mac
items: Mac: moving between screens is quicker, most of all in Native and after you've opened Settings.

notes.title: Faster look switching
items: Mac: switching between Verbose style and Native is faster while the Settings window is closed.

notes.title: Faster with big libraries
items: Verbose stays responsive while a file transcribes, and opens faster when you have a large library.

notes.title: Settings and Edit Home
items: Edit Home: show, hide, and drag to reorder Home's sections, including the new Last dictation, Projects, Moments, and Queue sections. Each look keeps its own layout on each device.

Edit Home: choose the four shortcut tiles from Dictate, Import, Live captions, Paste a link, Search, Moments, Queue, Dictations, Dictionary, and Projects, plus What's playing on iPhone and App audio and the Thought pad on Mac. Drag them into the order you want.
Edit Home: set each section to Compact, a slim row, or Large, the full card.
iPhone: tap Edit Home at the end of Home to change it. Changes show on Home right away.
Customize Home in Settings › Personalization and preferences opens the same Edit Home list on iPhone and Mac.
Mac: click Edit Home at the end of Home, or choose View › Edit Home. Each section gets an outline and a name, and the list of sections opens beside Home.
In Native, the Record section starts hidden because the floating record button stands in for it. The floating button stays on Home whether or not you show the section.
iPhone: Home's sections appear at once instead of rising in one by one.

Settings has seven groups on iPhone and Mac: Personalization and preferences, Recording and transcription, Dictation and keyboard, Sync and storage, Account and plan, Support and feedback, and Features. Each row shows its value, and search finds every setting in its new place.
iPhone: switches you rarely change move one level down, onto the Speakers, More transcription options, Cloud cleanup, and Welcome tour pages. Limit animation is a switch on the Settings page itself.
iPhone: Settings › Widgets and controls and Settings › Shortcuts and Siri list what Verbose offers and how to add it.
iPhone: tap the version at the bottom of Settings to see what's new. Cloud cleanup on the You page opens its Settings page.

Mac: the Settings sidebar has 12 panes, each with an icon. The Ribbon, the notch, and the floating button share one pane, as do Meetings and Live captions, and Watched folders and Export. Click the version at the foot of the sidebar to see what's new.
Mac: Settings › Features has the welcome tour, the widgets, and a button that opens Shortcuts.

notes.title: Widgets, Premium Native, and fixes
items: Mac: the Native look has a warmer, more polished design: a warm background, gradient cards for This week, your stats, and summaries, and a floating record button on Home and the Library.

Mac: in the Native look, the Library lists recordings with a preview beside them. Click to see the summary, double-click or press Return to open, and press Space to play. To see the table, choose More › View as Table.
Mac: in the Native look, a transcript shows its summary, moments, and speakers beside the text, the player has a Follow button, and Back and Forward are in the toolbar.
Mac: in the Native look, switching screens and opening transcripts take much less time.
Changing the look while a transcript is open no longer stops its audio or turns off skipping sponsor reads.
Opening one transcript from another keeps skipping its sponsor reads.
Mac: buttons in the accent color use black text in dark mode, so they're easier to read.
iPhone: the Native look becomes Premium Native, with a warm page and a soft glow, gradient cards in Verbose's colors, big rounded numbers, and recordings shown with a preview and a play button.
iPhone: in Native, a record button floats above the tab bar on Home and Library. Tap it to record a voice note, or touch and hold it for Dictate, Live captions, and Import.

iPhone: in Native, the recorder fills the screen with a large timer and a live waveform, and Mark moment saves bookmarks while you talk. When you stop, a sheet shows the transcription's progress and lets you choose the kind and the project.
iPhone: in Native, You shows your week, your year, and a calendar with a dot on each day you recorded, with no streak to keep.
iPhone: in Native, the transcript's summary shows on a persimmon card with its moments and speakers, and the player sits on glass above the tab bar.
iPhone: in Native, Settings › Appearance can bring back the Record card on Home.
New widgets: Record and Dictate, Recent recordings, This week, and Quick capture. They follow the look you choose in Verbose, and Recent recordings opens a transcript when you tap it.
iPhone: add them to the Home Screen, the Lock Screen (Record and Dictate), and StandBy. Record starts a voice note right where you are when iOS allows it, and otherwise opens Verbose to record.
iPhone: Control Center has Record voice note and Dictate controls.
Mac: add the widgets to your desktop. Quick capture opens the Thought pad, and Dictate types into the app in front.
iPhone: the speed fixes, bug fixes, and smoother look changes from Mac build 208.

notes.title: Faster screens and fixes (Mac)
items: Mac: choosing a look shows a short card while Verbose changes to it, and the change takes less time. On iPhone, this arrived in build 207.
Mac: screens appear at once when you switch to them, without sections fading in one by one, and Home's icons arrive drawn. They draw again when you point at them.
Mac: switching screens and opening a transcript do less work, so the app keeps up while something transcribes or plays.
Home's greeting and dates follow the clock while Verbose transcribes, plays, or dictates. On iPhone, You's dates do too.
Importing a damaged MP4 or M4A file no longer closes Verbose.
Mac: the thought pad's Send button names the app you switch to right away, and the pad stops checking once you close it.
Mac: on the You page, Cloud cleanup shows whether it's on and opens its own setting.
A long file that starts transcribing as Verbose opens keeps its saved progress, so if Verbose quits unexpectedly, the file picks up where it left off.

notes.title: Smoother look changes (iPhone)
items: Choosing a look shows a short card while Verbose changes to it, and the change takes less time.
iPhone: after you change the look, you stay on the same tab and screen, and Library keeps your search and filter.
iPhone: Home and Library switch fully to the Native look, and tags, categories, sponsor rows, and Settings cards match it. On Mac, these arrived in build 206.

notes.title: Native look fixes (Mac)
items: Tags, categories, and sponsor rows match the Native look.
Home and Library switch fully to the Native look.

notes.title: Version notes
items: Tap the version at the bottom of Settings to see what changed in each build. It's also in Settings › Support › What's new.
Mac: choose Verbose › What's New…, or open Settings › What's new.
After an update, Home shows a short note about the new build once. Tap it to read more, or close it.
Mac: the update window lists what's new in the build it offers.

notes.title: Two looks
items: New Native look on iPhone and Mac: a stock Apple style with a persimmon accent. Choose it in Settings › Appearance on iPhone or Settings › General on Mac, or when you first set up Verbose.
The Verbose keyboard follows the look you choose on iPhone.

notes.title: Automatic updates on Mac
items: The Mac app updates itself. New builds show up with Install and Relaunch, or choose Verbose › Check for Updates.

notes.title: Keyboard sessions, the notch, and the scrubber
items: With no session running, the keyboard shows Start a session, which opens Verbose straight into one. A card shows how to get back to the app you were in.
Getting ready: the first dictation shows that the speech model is loading instead of looking stuck. Verbose also loads it ahead of time when you open the app.
Keyboard sessions can last 10 minutes to 4 hours, or until you end them. The default is 2 hours.
A phone or FaceTime call pauses a session, and it resumes when the call ends.
When a session ends on its own, the Dynamic Island keeps a Restart button for 15 minutes.
Mac: the notch style now hangs over the menu bar, fully visible.
Mac: Verbose no longer asks for speech recognition at launch.
iPhone: the transcript scrubber now matches where you are in the recording, uses the brand's voice bars and speaker colors, and hides the system scroll bar.

notes.title: New ways to dictate
items: Mac: choose where dictation shows in Settings › Dictation: Ribbon, Notch, or Floating button. The notch style grows out of the MacBook notch; Macs without one get a pill at the top center.
Mac: a new floating dictation button with four looks and three sizes.
Mac: a new hotkey picker: Fn or Globe, Right ⌘, Right ⌥, a shortcut you record, or a mouse side button, with hold to talk or press to start and stop.
Mac: live words while you record a voice note.
iPhone: a new Dynamic Island and Lock Screen design for keyboard sessions.
iPhone: change the keyboard's dictate button size, position, and style in Settings › Keyboard.
iPhone: choose what the Action button does.
iPhone: hold the right edge of a long transcript and drag to scrub through it.

notes.title: Sponsors, speaker names, and YouTube on iPhone
items: Sponsor reads in podcasts fold into one row, playback skips them, and summaries and exports leave them out. Turn skipping off in Settings.
Suggested speaker names, from what people say, the link's channel and title, and voices you've named before. Tap Use to accept one.
YouTube links transcribe on iPhone with the right length, the channel, and the upload date.
Speaker changes line up with the ends of sentences.
Tags wrap onto more lines instead of running off the screen.

notes.title: Polish
items: iPhone: the record button on Home is centered on its rings.

notes.title: Speakers and categories
items: New categories: Podcast, Video, Talk, and Interview. Links and imported files are no longer labeled Meeting.
Main speaker only no longer hides people in links, imported files, and meetings.
Only one device transcribes each link, and both devices end up with the same copy.
Your TestFlight builds can transcribe YouTube links on iPhone.

notes.title: Opens even when iCloud is busy
items: Verbose no longer waits on iCloud to open. After an iOS update, it opens right away and loads the rest in the background.

notes.title: Faster
items: Links, Library, and You open faster, and rows no longer check the disk on every redraw.
Launch work moved out of the way, so the app is ready sooner.
Smoother scrolling in Moments on iPhone.

notes.title: Lighter keyboard
items: The keyboard redraws far less while you dictate, and live corrections stay fast on long dictations.
About 1,000 lines of unused code removed.

notes.title: Security
items: The Lock Screen widget and Tap to restart ask before recording, and the Action button needs Face ID when your iPhone is locked.
iCloud sync is off for new installs until you turn it on.
Safer handling of links, downloaded files, and synced data on Mac and iPhone.

notes.title: Earlier builds
items: The website-style redesign on Mac and iPhone.
The Verbose keyboard with Home, Typing, and Listening modes, and a dark mode that matches Apple's keyboard.
Import videos from Photos, including saved TikToks.
Cleaned transcripts no longer add speaker labels that weren't there.
A You page on iPhone.
